questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho's neighbours leave their dog tied up all day with no shade or water. What should she do?
options: Tell a parent or report it to the SPCA — this is neglect
questions.expected: Tell a parent or report it to the SPCA — this is neglect
questions.memo: Neglect is cruelty too. SPCA can investigate, advise the owners, and rescue the dog if needed. Reports save lives.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do if you find an injured wild animal.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if you find an injured wild animal.
options: Don't touch it — wild animals can bite when scared
Contact the SPCA, vet, or wildlife rescue
Stay back and wait for help
questions.expected: Don't touch it — wild animals can bite when scared,Tell an adult,Contact the SPCA, vet, or wildlife rescue,Stay back and wait for help
questions.memo: Don't touch (rabies, bites, stress) → adult → professional rescue → stay back. The animal needs experts, not us.

questions.question: True or false: Caring for animals teaches us how to care for people too.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Caring for animals teaches us how to care for people too.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Empathy practised on animals grows into empathy for people. Studies link kindness to animals with kindness in general.

questions.question: Why are 'puppy mills' (mass dog breeding for profit) considered cruel?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are 'puppy mills' — where dogs are mass-bred for profit — considered cruel?
options: Dogs are often kept in dirty crowded cages with no proper care or love
questions.expected: Dogs are often kept in dirty crowded cages with no proper care or love
questions.memo: Puppy mills prioritise profit over animal welfare. Adopting from SPCA or proper breeders helps shut them down.

questions.question: Tell me one thing a pet needs every day.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing a pet needs every day.
questions.expected: Fresh clean water
questions.memo: Good answers: fresh water, food, exercise, attention, safe shelter, clean space, sometimes a walk or play.

questions.question: Karabo wants to volunteer to help animals. Where could she start?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo wants to volunteer to help animals. Where could she start?
options: At a local SPCA, animal rescue or shelter — they often welcome young volunteers with adult help
questions.expected: At a local SPCA, animal rescue or shelter — they often welcome young volunteers with adult help
questions.memo: Shelters often have volunteer programmes — walking dogs, socialising cats, fundraising. Adults must usually supervise children.

questions.question: Why is it important to STERILISE (spay/neuter) pets?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to sterilise — spay or neuter — pets?
options: It prevents unwanted puppies and kittens, many of which end up homeless
questions.expected: It prevents unwanted puppies and kittens, many of which end up homeless
questions.memo: Many SA pet welfare problems start with overpopulation. Sterilisation reduces the number of unwanted animals. Free or low-cost programmes exist.

questions.question: When a pet is in pain or very old, the kindest decision is sometimes:
questions.ruby_prompt: When a pet is in pain or very old, the kindest decision is sometimes:
options: Speaking to a vet about end-of-life care, including humane euthanasia if suffering is severe
questions.expected: Speaking to a vet about end-of-life care, including humane euthanasia if suffering is severe
questions.memo: When suffering can't be eased, ending it humanely is sometimes the kindest gift. Vets help families through these hard decisions.

questions.question: The deepest reason to care for animals is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the deepest reason to care for animals?
options: They feel, they depend on us, and how we treat them says who we are
questions.expected: They feel, they depend on us, and how we treat them says who we are
questions.memo: How a society treats its animals reflects its character. Mahatma Gandhi said this. So did many religious teachers. Care reveals us.

LS.L6.PSW.T10.title: Caring for people
LS.L6.PSW.T10.description: Considering others' needs and views; communicating own views and needs without hurting others; acts of kindness.
LS.L6.PSW.T10.recovery_strategy: Affirm both sides — caring for others doesn't mean forgetting yourself. Practice 'kind AND honest' communication.

questions.question: What does 'caring for others' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does caring for others mean?
options: Noticing what they need or feel, and showing kindness in real ways
questions.expected: Noticing what they need or feel, and showing kindness in real ways
questions.memo: Caring is noticing + acting. Both halves matter. A noticed-but-untouched need is not caring.

questions.question: Which is an act of kindness?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is an act of kindness?
options: Sharing your lunch with a hungry classmate
questions.expected: Sharing your lunch with a hungry classmate
questions.memo: Small acts of kindness are huge. Sharing food, holding a door, listening — these are real care.

questions.question: True or false: Caring for others doesn't mean ignoring your own needs.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Caring for others doesn't mean ignoring your own needs.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: True. Healthy caring includes yourself. Burned-out caregivers can't keep caring. You matter too.

questions.question: Lerato's grandmother is sad after her husband died. The most caring thing Lerato can do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerata's grandmother is grieving her husband. What's the most caring thing Lerata can do?
options: Spend time with her, listen, do small chores — be present
questions.expected: Spend time with her, listen, do small chores — be present
questions.memo: Grief needs presence more than fixing. Showing up is the gift. Small chores ease the weight.

questions.question: Why is LISTENING such an important way to care?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is listening such an important way to care for someone?
options: People often need to feel heard more than they need to be told what to do
questions.expected: People often need to feel heard more than they need to be told what to do
questions.memo: Most pain is eased by feeling truly heard. Advice often comes too quickly. Listening first, advice rarely.

questions.question: Which is a way to share YOUR view kindly?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to share your view kindly?
options: 'I see it differently — for me it feels like...' (I-statements)
questions.expected: 'I see it differently — for me it feels like...' (I-statements)
questions.memo: I-statements share without attacking. The other person can hear them. Insults close ears.

questions.question: True or false: Caring people sometimes have to say HARD truths kindly.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Caring people sometimes have to say hard truths kindly.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Love sometimes says things the person doesn't want to hear — but says them gently and with care. Honesty + kindness.

questions.question: Sipho's friend is sad but doesn't say why. The caring thing is to:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's friend is sad but won't say why. What's the caring thing for Sipho to do?
options: Stay nearby, let her know he's there when she's ready to talk
questions.expected: Stay nearby, let her know he's there when she's ready to talk
questions.memo: Presence without pressure. Caring sometimes means giving someone space to come to you. Patience is part of care.

questions.question: An OLDER neighbour can't carry her shopping. The caring response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Your older neighbour can't carry her shopping. What's the caring response?
options: Offer to carry it for her, without making her feel weak
questions.expected: Offer to carry it for her, without making her feel weak
questions.memo: Offering preserves dignity. 'Can I give you a hand?' is gentler than just taking over. People keep their pride.

questions.question: Why is it good to ASK before helping?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it good to ask before helping someone?
options: They may want different help — and asking respects their choice
questions.expected: They may want different help — and asking respects their choice
questions.memo: Asking respects autonomy. Sometimes people want help, sometimes just company, sometimes nothing. Ask before assuming.

questions.question: Mpho disagrees with her friend's idea for a project. Caring communication looks like:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho disagrees with her friend's idea for a project. What does caring communication look like?
options: 'I see what you mean. I see it a bit differently — here's why...' — kind and honest
questions.expected: 'I see what you mean. I see it a bit differently — here's why...' — kind and honest
questions.memo: Caring doesn't mean dishonest. The skill is HOW you disagree — acknowledge, share, suggest. Friendship survives honesty when wrapped in respect.

questions.question: What is COMPASSION FATIGUE?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is compassion fatigue?
options: When you've cared so much for others that you feel drained yourself
questions.expected: When you've cared so much for others that you feel drained yourself
questions.memo: Even kind people get tired. Compassion fatigue means we need to recharge — sleep, rest, our own friends. Caring well includes self-care.

questions.question: Karabo wants to help a homeless family in her area. A real first step is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo wants to help a homeless family she sees regularly. What's a real first step?
options: Ask a parent or community group about a safe, sustained way to help
questions.expected: Ask a parent or community group about a safe, sustained way to help
questions.memo: Real help is steady, not flashy. Working with a church, NGO or shelter scales kindness safely and effectively.

questions.question: Put these in order for helping a friend in distress.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for helping a friend in distress.
options: If needed, gently encourage them to get help from a trusted adult
questions.expected: Notice that they're struggling,Be present without judgement,Listen,If needed, gently encourage them to get help from a trusted adult
questions.memo: Notice → presence → listen → encourage adult help. Not fixing, not advising — just walking beside.

questions.question: Tell me one act of kindness you could do this week.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one act of kindness you could do this week.
questions.expected: Help my mom with the dishes without being asked
questions.memo: Good answers: help at home, sit with a lonely classmate, write a kind note, share, listen, do a chore for someone tired.

questions.question: True or false: Caring for ourselves is part of being able to care for others.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Caring for ourselves is part of being able to care for others.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. You can't pour from an empty cup. Sleep, food, friendship, rest — these fuel the kindness you give.

questions.question: When a friend is in serious trouble (depressed, suicidal, in danger), the BEST move is:
questions.ruby_prompt: When a friend is in serious trouble — depressed, suicidal, or in real danger — what's the best move?
options: Tell a trusted adult right away — bigger problems need adult help
questions.expected: Tell a trusted adult right away — bigger problems need adult help
questions.memo: Some secrets are too heavy. A friend's life is more important than a promise. Adults (counsellors, SADAG 0800 567 567) can save lives.

questions.question: Why are GROUPS of caring people more powerful than one?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are groups of caring people often more powerful than one person caring alone?
options: More hands, more ideas, more sustainability — and no one burns out alone
Only one person can care at a time
questions.expected: More hands, more ideas, more sustainability — and no one burns out alone
questions.memo: Care scales in community. Soup kitchens, book clubs, churches, NGOs all multiply individual care. SA has a strong tradition of this.

questions.question: What's the DIFFERENCE between caring and pleasing everyone?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the difference between caring and pleasing everyone?
options: Caring includes honesty and your own needs; pleasing forgets both
questions.expected: Caring includes honesty and your own needs; pleasing forgets both
questions.memo: Pleasing = saying yes to everything, even when it harms you. Caring includes honest no, real boundaries, and yourself.

questions.question: The deepest truth about caring for people is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the deepest truth about caring for people?
options: Small steady acts of kindness change lives — including the giver's
questions.expected: Small steady acts of kindness change lives — including the giver's
questions.memo: The science is clear: kindness changes BOTH brains — the receiver's and the giver's. Daily small acts grow a kinder world.

LS.L6.PSW.T11.title: Nation-building and cultural heritage
LS.L6.PSW.T11.description: How cultural heritage unifies the nation; national symbols (flag, anthem, coat of arms); national days (Human Rights, Freedom, Heritage, Reconciliation, Children's, Women's, Africa, Mandela Day).
LS.L6.PSW.T11.recovery_strategy: Stay factual and balanced. SA's diversity is its strength. Help the learner see the national symbols as inclusive — for ALL South Africans.

questions.question: What is 'nation-building'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is nation-building?
options: Working together to build a strong, united country across all communities
questions.expected: Working together to build a strong, united country across all communities
questions.memo: Nation-building draws diverse people together into shared purpose. SA's post-1994 project is one of the world's most famous examples.

questions.question: What does CULTURAL HERITAGE mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does cultural heritage mean?
options: The traditions, languages, customs and history passed down through a community
questions.expected: The traditions, languages, customs and history passed down through a community
questions.memo: Heritage = what we inherit — language, music, dance, food, beliefs, stories. SA's heritage is plural and rich.

questions.question: How many official languages does South Africa have?
questions.ruby_prompt: How many official languages does South Africa have?
options: 11 — soon to be 12 with South African Sign Language
questions.expected: 11 — soon to be 12 with South African Sign Language
questions.memo: 11 official languages, with SA Sign Language being added. This linguistic diversity is part of SA's identity.

questions.question: The SA flag has how many colours?
questions.ruby_prompt: The South African flag has how many colours?
options: 6 — black, gold, green, white, red, blue
questions.expected: 6 — black, gold, green, white, red, blue
questions.memo: 6 colours arranged to show convergence — the Y-shape represents diverse paths joining as one. Designed by Frederick Brownell.

questions.question: What does the Y-SHAPE of the SA flag symbolise?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the Y-shape on the South African flag symbolise?
options: Convergence — different paths joining into one nation
questions.expected: Convergence — different paths joining into one nation
questions.memo: The Y meets and flows together — a national symbol of unity in diversity. From two paths into one road.

questions.question: The SA national anthem combines:
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the South African national anthem combine?
options: Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika and Die Stem — and uses multiple languages
questions.expected: Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika and Die Stem — and uses multiple languages
questions.memo: Our anthem joins two historical anthems and uses isiXhosa, isiZulu, Sesotho, Afrikaans and English. It carries our complicated, hopeful story.

questions.question: Heritage Day is on:
questions.ruby_prompt: Heritage Day is on what date?
questions.expected: 24 September
questions.memo: 24 September — also known by many as Braai Day. The day celebrates SA's cultural diversity.

questions.question: What does HUMAN RIGHTS DAY (21 March) remember?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does Human Rights Day on 21 March remember?
options: The Sharpeville massacre of 1960 — and the human rights of all South Africans
questions.expected: The Sharpeville massacre of 1960 — and the human rights of all South Africans
questions.memo: On 21 March 1960, police killed 69 people peacefully protesting pass laws. The day honours them and our commitment to rights for all.

questions.question: FREEDOM DAY (27 April) marks:
questions.ruby_prompt: What does Freedom Day on 27 April mark?
options: The first democratic elections in South Africa in 1994
questions.expected: The first democratic elections in South Africa in 1994
questions.memo: 27 April 1994 — for the first time, all South African adults could vote. It is the birthday of our democracy.

questions.question: WOMEN'S DAY (9 August) honours:
questions.ruby_prompt: What does Women's Day on 9 August honour?
options: The 1956 march of 20 000 women to the Union Buildings against pass laws
questions.expected: The 1956 march of 20 000 women to the Union Buildings against pass laws
questions.memo: 9 August 1956 — women of all races marched against pass laws. 'Wathint' abafazi, wathint' imbokodo' — you strike a woman, you strike a rock.

questions.question: RECONCILIATION DAY (16 December) is about:
questions.ruby_prompt: What is Reconciliation Day on 16 December about?
options: Healing past divisions and building one nation from many
questions.expected: Healing past divisions and building one nation from many
questions.memo: 16 December — once a contested day in apartheid times — became a day to heal and unite. A direct nation-building day.

questions.question: MANDELA DAY (18 July) asks every person to:
questions.ruby_prompt: What does Mandela Day on 18 July ask every person to do?
options: Give 67 minutes of service to others — one minute for each year of his service
questions.expected: Give 67 minutes of service to others — one minute for each year of his service
questions.memo: 67 minutes for the 67 years Madiba spent fighting for justice. People plant trees, feed the hungry, paint schools, visit the lonely.

questions.question: True or false: Cultural diversity is one of SA's greatest strengths.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Cultural diversity is one of South Africa's greatest strengths.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Our diversity is real, complicated and rich — a source of strength when we treat each other with dignity.

questions.question: AFRICA DAY (25 May) celebrates:
questions.ruby_prompt: What does Africa Day on 25 May celebrate?
options: The founding of what is now the African Union — and African unity
questions.expected: The founding of what is now the African Union — and African unity
questions.memo: 25 May 1963 — the Organisation of African Unity (now AU) was formed. SA celebrates being part of the African family of nations.

questions.question: CHILDREN'S DAY (1 June or first Saturday of November) is about:
questions.ruby_prompt: What is Children's Day about?
options: Recognising children's rights and the importance of their wellbeing
questions.expected: Recognising children's rights and the importance of their wellbeing
questions.memo: International Children's Day honours every child's rights — to education, safety, family, health, dignity.

questions.question: Sipho's family is going to a Heritage Day event. The most ENRICHING thing he could do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's family is going to a Heritage Day event. What's the most enriching thing he could do there?
options: Try food, music or stories from cultures different to his own — alongside his own
Stick only to what he already knows
questions.expected: Try food, music or stories from cultures different to his own — alongside his own
questions.memo: Heritage Day is for tasting other people's heritage too. His own + new = the SA way.

questions.question: The COAT OF ARMS motto is in:
questions.ruby_prompt: The South African coat of arms motto !ke e꞉/xarra //ke is in:
options: /Xam — an extinct language of the San people. It means 'Diverse people unite'
questions.expected: /Xam — an extinct language of the San people. It means 'Diverse people unite'
questions.memo: The motto honours SA's oldest people — the San — whose language /Xam is no longer spoken. The phrase calls all of us to unity.

questions.question: Tell me one national day and what it celebrates.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one South African national day and what it celebrates.
questions.expected: Freedom Day (27 April) — our first democratic election in 1994
questions.memo: Good answers: Human Rights Day (21 March), Freedom Day (27 April), Workers Day (1 May), Youth Day (16 June), Mandela Day (18 July), Women's Day (9 August), Heritage Day (24 September), Reconciliation Day (16 December).

questions.question: Why do we celebrate national days as A NATION?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we celebrate national days as a nation?
options: Shared memory and shared values keep us connected as one country
questions.expected: Shared memory and shared values keep us connected as one country
questions.memo: National days are shared stories. Honouring them keeps SA from forgetting where we came from and where we're going.

questions.question: The strongest way for YOU to contribute to nation-building is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the strongest way for you to contribute to nation-building?
options: Living the values daily — respect, honesty, kindness, working hard, helping others
Waiting for grown-ups to do it
questions.expected: Living the values daily — respect, honesty, kindness, working hard, helping others
questions.memo: Nations are built one person, one day at a time. Daily choices add up to the country we become.

LS.L6.PSW.T12.title: Gender stereotyping, sexism and abuse
LS.L6.PSW.T12.description: Definitions; effects of gender stereotyping and sexism on personal and social relationships; effects of gender-based abuse; dealing with stereotyping, sexism and abuse.
LS.L6.PSW.T12.recovery_strategy: Reinforce: girls and boys are equal under the SA Constitution. Gender-based violence is a serious crime. Help paths include Childline 116 and the GBV Command Centre 0800 428 428.

questions.question: What is a 'gender stereotype'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a gender stereotype?
options: A fixed idea about what boys/men or girls/women should do or be
questions.expected: A fixed idea about what boys/men or girls/women should do or be
questions.memo: Gender stereotypes are 'all boys are X, all girls are Y'. Real people are far more varied than the boxes.

questions.question: What is 'sexism'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is sexism?
options: Treating someone unfairly because of their gender
questions.expected: Treating someone unfairly because of their gender
questions.memo: Sexism is discrimination based on gender. It can show in jobs, pay, opportunities, or how we speak about people.

questions.question: True or false: Sexism is against the SA Constitution.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Sexism is against the South African Constitution.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Section 9 of the Constitution bans unfair discrimination on the basis of gender. Equal rights = constitutional law.

questions.question: Which is a HARMFUL gender stereotype?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a harmful gender stereotype?
questions.expected: 'Boys shouldn't cry'
questions.memo: 'Boys shouldn't cry' bottles up boys' feelings, sometimes leading to depression or anger problems later. All people cry — it's healthy.

questions.question: How does gender stereotyping AFFECT girls?
questions.ruby_prompt: How does gender stereotyping affect girls?
options: It can limit their dreams — many girls are still told certain careers aren't for them
It helps them in every way
questions.expected: It can limit their dreams — many girls are still told certain careers aren't for them
questions.memo: Stereotypes close doors. 'Girls don't do engineering/maths/sport' has cost SA generations of talent. Things are changing.

questions.question: How does gender stereotyping AFFECT boys?
questions.ruby_prompt: How does gender stereotyping affect boys?
options: It can stop boys showing feelings or asking for help — which harms their mental health
It helps boys in every way
questions.expected: It can stop boys showing feelings or asking for help — which harms their mental health
questions.memo: 'Be a man' = bottle up feelings. This is linked to higher male suicide rates. Boys deserve to feel and ask for help too.

questions.question: What is GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE (GBV)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is gender-based violence — GBV?
options: Violence aimed at someone because of their gender — especially against women and girls
questions.expected: Violence aimed at someone because of their gender — especially against women and girls
questions.memo: GBV is a serious crime. It includes physical, sexual, emotional and economic violence — and SA has very high rates.

questions.question: True or false: Gender-based violence is NEVER the victim's fault.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Gender-based violence is never the victim's fault.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Always true. No clothing, no behaviour, no relationship makes someone deserve violence. The responsibility is always the abuser's.

questions.question: Where can a person experiencing gender-based abuse get help in SA?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where can a person experiencing gender-based abuse get help in SA?
options: GBV Command Centre 0800 428 428, Childline 116, SAPS 10111, a clinic, a counsellor
questions.expected: GBV Command Centre 0800 428 428, Childline 116, SAPS 10111, a clinic, a counsellor
questions.memo: Multiple free help paths. The GBV Command Centre (0800 428 428) is 24/7. Childline 116 helps children. Police: 10111.

questions.question: Lerato hears 'boys will be boys' used to excuse harmful behaviour. The truth is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato hears 'boys will be boys' used to excuse harmful behaviour. What's the truth?
options: Harmful behaviour is not 'natural' to boys. Boys can and should be held to the same standards as anyone
questions.expected: Harmful behaviour is not 'natural' to boys. Boys can and should be held to the same standards as anyone
questions.memo: 'Boys will be boys' excuses behaviour that should never be excused. It also insults the many boys who DO behave well.

questions.question: Sipho sees his older brother shouting at his sister. What should Sipho do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho sees his older brother shouting threats at his sister. What should Sipho do?
options: Get to safety, tell a parent or trusted adult — this could escalate into abuse
Tell his sister it's her fault
questions.expected: Get to safety, tell a parent or trusted adult — this could escalate into abuse
questions.memo: Threatening behaviour can be the start of abuse. Early intervention saves lives. Adults can act — keep yourself safe first.

questions.question: Which is a SIGN of an abusive relationship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign of an abusive relationship?
options: Controlling behaviour — telling someone what to wear, who to see, isolating them
questions.expected: Controlling behaviour — telling someone what to wear, who to see, isolating them
questions.memo: Control is often the first sign of abuse. It comes before physical violence in many cases. Isolation, monitoring, jealousy as 'love'.

questions.question: Mpho's classmate boys make comments about her body. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho's classmates — some boys — make comments about her body. What should she do?
options: Tell them to stop, then tell a teacher and a parent if it continues
questions.expected: Tell them to stop, then tell a teacher and a parent if it continues
questions.memo: Verbal harassment is real harm. Speaking up is right. Adults can deal with it through school discipline systems.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do if you experience harassment or abuse.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if you experience harassment or abuse.
options: Call a help line (Childline 116 or GBV 0800 428 428)
Get ongoing support — counsellor or trusted person
questions.expected: Get to a safe place,Tell a trusted adult,Call a help line (Childline 116 or GBV 0800 428 428),Get ongoing support — counsellor or trusted person
questions.memo: Safety → tell → help line → ongoing care. Each step gets you further from harm and closer to healing.

questions.question: True or false: Boys and men can ALSO be victims of gender-based violence.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Boys and men can also be victims of gender-based violence.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Although women and girls are more often targeted, boys and men also experience GBV. They deserve help too — without shame.

questions.question: Tell me one stereotype you'd like to challenge.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one gender stereotype you'd like to challenge.
questions.expected: That girls can't be good at maths or science
questions.memo: Good answers: any stereotype the learner is ready to push back on. The naming is the first step. Living the counter-example is the second.

questions.question: Why is GENDER EQUALITY good for ALL of society?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is gender equality good for all of society — not just for women?
options: Everyone benefits — talents are fully used, families are healthier, violence drops
questions.expected: Everyone benefits — talents are fully used, families are healthier, violence drops
questions.memo: Equality lifts the whole boat. Better economies, healthier families, less violence, more democracy. SA's research backs this up.

questions.question: Karabo's friend is in an abusive relationship and says, 'He loves me, he just gets angry.' Karabo should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's friend is in an abusive relationship and says 'He loves me, he just gets angry.' What should Karabo do?
options: Stay her friend, share that real love isn't violent, and tell a trusted adult
Believe her friend that it's love
questions.expected: Stay her friend, share that real love isn't violent, and tell a trusted adult
questions.memo: Loyalty + gentle truth-telling + adult help. Abuse victims often defend their abusers; sustained friendship and clear info eventually help.

questions.question: Which is a SIGN that a society is moving toward gender equality?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign that a society is moving toward gender equality?
options: More women in leadership, more men in caregiving, more reporting of GBV and consequences
questions.expected: More women in leadership, more men in caregiving, more reporting of GBV and consequences
questions.memo: Signs of progress: leadership balance, caring roles shared, abuse taken seriously by courts. SA is in the middle of this work.

questions.question: The most important thing to remember about gender-based abuse is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important thing to remember about gender-based abuse?
options: It is never the victim's fault, help is real and free, and silence keeps it going
questions.expected: It is never the victim's fault, help is real and free, and silence keeps it going
questions.memo: Three truths. Not your fault. Help is real (0800 428 428 / 116). Speaking up — yours or someone else's — breaks the cycle.

LS.L6.PSW.T13.title: Basic first aid
LS.L6.PSW.T13.description: Basic first aid for cuts and grazes, burns, scalds and sunburn, stings and bites, bruises, poisoning, bleeding, choking.
LS.L6.PSW.T13.recovery_strategy: Confidence matters. Walk through each technique calmly. Reinforce: when in doubt, get an adult or call 10177. Some basic skills save lives.

questions.question: What is FIRST AID?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is first aid?
options: The first care given to someone who is hurt or sick, before professional help arrives
questions.expected: The first care given to someone who is hurt or sick, before professional help arrives
questions.memo: First aid is what we do RIGHT NOW. It can save a life or stop an injury from getting worse before paramedics arrive.

questions.question: What is the SA AMBULANCE number?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is the South African ambulance/fire emergency number?
questions.memo: 10177 = ambulance/fire. 10111 = police. 112 from a mobile connects to emergency services. Memorise these.

questions.question: For a SMALL CUT or graze, the first steps are:
questions.ruby_prompt: For a small cut or graze, the first steps are:
options: Wash with clean water, gently dab dry, apply a plaster (band-aid)
questions.expected: Wash with clean water, gently dab dry, apply a plaster (band-aid)
questions.memo: Clean water removes germs. A plaster keeps the wound clean while it heals. Check for tetanus shot status with a parent or clinic.

questions.question: For a MINOR BURN (like from a hot pan), do:
questions.ruby_prompt: For a minor burn — like from a hot pan — what should you do?
options: Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 10 minutes
Put butter or toothpaste on it
questions.expected: Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 10 minutes
questions.memo: Cool water stops the burn from going deeper into the skin. NEVER use butter, oil or ice. 10+ minutes makes a real difference.

questions.question: True or false: Big burns need a hospital, not home first aid.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Big burns need a hospital, not just home first aid.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Cool the burn briefly, but get to a hospital. Big burns can cause shock and need professional care. Call 10177.

questions.question: For SUNBURN, the first aid is:
questions.ruby_prompt: For sunburn, what's the first aid?
options: Get out of the sun, cool the skin gently, drink water, use aloe or after-sun lotion
questions.expected: Get out of the sun, cool the skin gently, drink water, use aloe or after-sun lotion
questions.memo: Shade, cool, hydrate, soothe. Severe sunburn (blisters) needs a clinic. Prevention is best: hat, sunscreen, shade.

questions.question: For a BEE STING, the first step is:
questions.ruby_prompt: For a bee sting, what's the first step?
options: Remove the sting by scraping (not squeezing) and wash with soap and water
questions.expected: Remove the sting by scraping (not squeezing) and wash with soap and water
questions.memo: Scraping removes the sting without pumping more venom. Wash, ice for swelling. Anyone who has trouble breathing → ambulance straight away.

questions.question: For a SNAKE BITE, the first move is:
questions.ruby_prompt: For a snake bite, what's the first move?
options: Keep the person calm and still, call 10177, get to a hospital with details of the snake if possible
Run as fast as you can
questions.expected: Keep the person calm and still, call 10177, get to a hospital with details of the snake if possible
questions.memo: Movement spreads venom. Calm + still + ambulance + describing the snake = best chance. Don't cut, suck or use tourniquets — outdated.

questions.question: For a BRUISE, the first aid is:
questions.ruby_prompt: For a bruise, what's the first aid?
options: Cold pack (or ice wrapped in cloth) for about 10–15 minutes
questions.expected: Cold pack (or ice wrapped in cloth) for about 10–15 minutes
questions.memo: Cold reduces swelling. Cloth between ice and skin (direct ice can damage skin). Repeat as needed in first 24 hours.

questions.question: If someone has swallowed POISON, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone has swallowed something poisonous, what should you do?
options: Call the Poisons Information Centre (0861 555 777) or 10177 immediately
questions.expected: Call the Poisons Information Centre (0861 555 777) or 10177 immediately
questions.memo: Do NOT make them vomit unless told to. Some poisons damage on the way back up. The Poisons line tells you exactly what to do for that substance.

questions.question: For HEAVY BLEEDING, the first action is:
questions.ruby_prompt: For heavy bleeding, what's the first action?
options: Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth and call 10177
questions.expected: Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth and call 10177
questions.memo: Direct pressure stops most bleeding. Keep pressing — don't keep checking. Get an ambulance. Use gloves if you have them (HIV risk).

questions.question: If someone is CHOKING and can still cough, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone is choking and can still cough, you should:
options: Encourage them to keep coughing — coughing can clear it
Hit them on the back hard
questions.expected: Encourage them to keep coughing — coughing can clear it
questions.memo: Coughing is the body's own first aid. If they can cough, breathe and speak, they're working it out. Stay close in case it gets worse.

questions.question: If someone is choking and CAN'T BREATHE or cough:
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone is choking and CAN'T breathe or cough at all, you should:
options: Get a grown-up immediately to do back blows and call 10177
questions.expected: Get a grown-up immediately to do back blows and call 10177
questions.memo: This is a real emergency. Adults can do back blows / abdominal thrusts. Children should focus on getting help fast.

questions.question: True or false: Knowing first aid can save a life.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Knowing first aid can save a life.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Many lives are lost not because help isn't available but because no one acted in those first crucial minutes. Knowing matters.

questions.question: What's in a basic FIRST AID KIT?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's in a basic first aid kit?
options: Plasters, bandages, antiseptic, gauze, gloves, scissors, basic painkillers
questions.expected: Plasters, bandages, antiseptic, gauze, gloves, scissors, basic painkillers
questions.memo: Every home should have a basic kit. Pharmacies sell pre-packed ones. Check expiry dates.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do at an accident scene.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do at the scene of an accident.
options: Check the scene is safe for you
Give first aid and stay until help arrives
questions.expected: Check the scene is safe for you,Check the injured person,Call 10177,Give first aid and stay until help arrives
questions.memo: Safe scene → check person → call → care. SCENE first — saving a life shouldn't cost yours. This is universal first aid order.

questions.question: Tell me one first aid action you know.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one first aid action you know.
questions.expected: Cool a burn under running water
questions.memo: Good answers: cool burns, wash cuts, ice bruises, call 10177, pressure on bleeding, scrape bee stings, get an adult.

questions.question: Lerato's friend just touched a hot stove. The first thing Lerato should do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerata's friend just touched a hot stove. What should Lerata do first?
options: Run the burn under cool water for 10+ minutes and tell a grown-up
questions.expected: Run the burn under cool water for 10+ minutes and tell a grown-up
questions.memo: Cool water is the gold standard. 10+ minutes makes a real difference to healing. Get an adult either way.

questions.question: True or false: When in doubt about an injury, calling for help is the right move.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: When in doubt about how serious an injury is, calling for help is the right move.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Better safe than sorry. 10177 dispatchers can advise even when not sending an ambulance.

questions.question: The most important rule in first aid is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important rule in first aid?
options: Stay calm, keep yourself safe, get help — and do what you can while you wait
questions.expected: Stay calm, keep yourself safe, get help — and do what you can while you wait
questions.memo: Calm + safe + help + act. Those four are the heart of first aid. Even children can save lives by following them.

LS.L6.PSW.T14.title: Food hygiene
LS.L6.PSW.T14.description: Safe and harmful ingredients, food preparation, food storage, food-borne diseases.
LS.L6.PSW.T14.recovery_strategy: Food hygiene is mostly practical habits. Walk the learner through the kitchen — clean, separate, cook, chill. Easy to remember once learned.

questions.question: Why is FOOD HYGIENE important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is food hygiene important?
options: Dirty food can make people very sick — sometimes seriously
It is a school rule only
questions.expected: Dirty food can make people very sick — sometimes seriously
questions.memo: Food poisoning kills thousands of children worldwide each year. Good food hygiene is one of the best protections a family has.

questions.question: Which is the FIRST step before preparing food?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the first step before preparing food?
options: Wash your hands with soap and water
questions.expected: Wash your hands with soap and water
questions.memo: Clean hands = safer food. Hands carry germs from everywhere. Wash before cooking, between raw and cooked, after the toilet, before eating.

questions.question: Why must RAW meat be kept SEPARATE from other food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why must raw meat be kept separate from other food?
options: Raw meat carries germs that can spread to other food and cause illness
questions.expected: Raw meat carries germs that can spread to other food and cause illness
questions.memo: Cross-contamination is a major cause of food poisoning. Separate boards, knives, surfaces for raw meat. Wash everything afterwards.

questions.question: True or false: You should COOK chicken until it's properly done in the middle.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You should cook chicken until it's properly cooked through in the middle.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Chicken often carries salmonella. Properly cooked = no pink, juices run clear, internal temperature above 75°C. Undercooked chicken makes you very sick.

questions.question: How should LEFTOVER food be stored?
questions.ruby_prompt: How should leftover food be stored?
options: Cool quickly and store in the fridge (covered) within 2 hours of cooking
Leave it on the counter overnight
questions.expected: Cool quickly and store in the fridge (covered) within 2 hours of cooking
questions.memo: Germs grow fastest at room temperature. Quick cooling + covered fridge = safe leftovers. Use within 2-3 days. Reheat thoroughly.

questions.question: Which is a FOOD-BORNE disease?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a food-borne disease — caused by germs from bad food?
options: Salmonella (often from raw chicken or eggs)
A headache from too much screen time
questions.expected: Salmonella (often from raw chicken or eggs)
questions.memo: Salmonella, E. coli, listeria are common food-borne germs. They cause diarrhoea, vomiting, fever — sometimes seriously so.

questions.question: Which is a sign that food has GONE BAD?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign that food has gone bad?
options: Strange smell, mould, slimy texture, unusual colour
questions.expected: Strange smell, mould, slimy texture, unusual colour
questions.memo: Trust your senses. If it smells, looks or feels wrong — throw it. The cost of throwing it is much less than the cost of food poisoning.

questions.question: Sipho is making sandwiches. He just touched raw chicken. What MUST he do next?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho is making sandwiches. He just touched raw chicken before making them. What MUST he do next?
options: Wash his hands with soap and water before touching anything else
Wipe his hands on a towel only
questions.expected: Wash his hands with soap and water before touching anything else
questions.memo: Soap + water + 20 seconds = safe hands. Towel-only doesn't remove germs from raw meat. Soap is the magic.

questions.question: Which is a SAFE TEMPERATURE for keeping food cold?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a safe temperature for keeping cold food cold?
questions.expected: Below 5°C in the fridge
questions.memo: Below 5°C slows germ growth dramatically. Keep your fridge at this temperature. Most home fridges are designed for it.

questions.question: Put these in order for safe food preparation.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for safe food preparation.
options: Clean the work surface and equipment
Keep raw meat separate from other food
Cook food properly and serve straight away or store
questions.expected: Wash hands,Clean the work surface and equipment,Keep raw meat separate from other food,Cook food properly and serve straight away or store
questions.memo: Clean → clean surfaces → separate → cook + serve/store. The 'four C's' of food safety: Clean, Cook, Chill, Cross-contamination avoided.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to LEAVE FOOD OUT in hot weather?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it dangerous to leave food out in hot weather?
options: Germs grow very quickly at warm temperatures, making food unsafe within hours
questions.expected: Germs grow very quickly at warm temperatures, making food unsafe within hours
questions.memo: Between 5°C and 60°C is the 'danger zone'. Germs double every 20 minutes. Hot SA summer days speed this up — fridge food fast.

questions.question: True or false: Smelling food is enough to tell if it's safe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Smelling food is enough to tell if it's safe.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: False. Some dangerous germs don't change the smell, look or taste of food. If in doubt, throw it out — especially raw or undercooked meat.

questions.question: Lerato spots that the milk has gone past its 'use by' date by 2 days. She should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerata sees the milk is 2 days past its 'use by' date. What should she do?
options: Don't use it — 'use by' is a safety date, not a suggestion
Add sugar to mask the taste
questions.expected: Don't use it — 'use by' is a safety date, not a suggestion
questions.memo: 'Use by' = safety. 'Best before' = quality. Use-by dates aren't suggestions for meat, fish, milk. Throw away.

questions.question: Which is a SYMPTOM of food poisoning?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a symptom of food poisoning?
questions.expected: Vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, stomach cramps
questions.memo: Symptoms appear hours to days after eating bad food. Hydrate (water, ORS), rest, see a doctor if severe or in small children.

questions.question: Why is HAND WASHING the most important food hygiene step?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is hand washing the most important food hygiene step?
options: Hands carry germs from many places straight onto food we then eat
questions.expected: Hands carry germs from many places straight onto food we then eat
questions.memo: Hands touch animals, money, toilets, doorknobs, then food. One hand wash interrupts thousands of germ journeys.

questions.question: Mpho is going to use eggs that have small cracks. She should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho is going to use eggs but they have small cracks. She should:
options: Throw them out — cracked shells let germs in
questions.expected: Throw them out — cracked shells let germs in
questions.memo: Eggshells protect against salmonella. A crack = the gate is open. Always use intact eggs.

questions.question: Tell me one rule of safe food storage.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one rule of safe food storage.
questions.expected: Keep raw meat covered on the bottom shelf of the fridge so it doesn't drip onto other food
questions.memo: Good answers: raw meat on bottom shelf (no drips), cool leftovers fast and fridge them, label dates, use first-in-first-out, throw if doubtful.

questions.question: True or false: Reheating food properly kills most germs.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Reheating food properly kills most germs.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Reheat until steaming hot all the way through (above 75°C). Don't reheat the same dish more than once.

questions.question: What's a good rule when in doubt about whether food is safe?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a good rule when in doubt about whether food is safe?
options: If in doubt, throw it out — your health is worth more than the food
Share it with friends to test
questions.expected: If in doubt, throw it out — your health is worth more than the food
questions.memo: A few rand of food < a hospital visit. The wise food handler errs on the side of caution.

questions.question: The big idea of food hygiene is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the big idea of food hygiene?
options: Clean, separate, cook, chill — four habits that prevent most food illness
Cooking everything for a long time
questions.expected: Clean, separate, cook, chill — four habits that prevent most food illness
questions.memo: The four C's of food safety: Clean, Cook, Chill, no Cross-contamination. Used worldwide by food safety bodies. Easy to remember.

LS.L6.PSW.T15.title: Communicable diseases
LS.L6.PSW.T15.description: Diseases such as mumps, tuberculosis, common colds, chickenpox, athlete's foot; causes, signs and symptoms, prevention strategies, available treatment.
LS.L6.PSW.T15.recovery_strategy: Stay factual. Prevention is empowering. Vaccinations and hygiene are real, free tools. Help the learner feel equipped, not anxious.

questions.question: What is a 'communicable disease'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a communicable disease?
options: A disease that can spread from one person to another
A disease only one person can have
questions.expected: A disease that can spread from one person to another
questions.memo: Communicable = contagious. Caused by germs (viruses, bacteria, fungi, parasites) that move from person to person.

questions.question: What causes a COMMON COLD?
questions.ruby_prompt: What causes a common cold?
options: A virus that spreads through coughs, sneezes and touched surfaces
questions.expected: A virus that spreads through coughs, sneezes and touched surfaces
questions.memo: Cold viruses spread through droplets and surfaces. Cold weather doesn't cause it — but people staying indoors close together does.

questions.question: How does CHICKENPOX spread?
questions.ruby_prompt: How does chickenpox spread?
options: Through the air (coughs/sneezes) and touching the rash blisters
questions.expected: Through the air (coughs/sneezes) and touching the rash blisters
questions.memo: Chickenpox is very contagious. Spreads days before the rash even appears. A vaccine exists.

questions.question: What's a common symptom of MUMPS?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a common symptom of mumps?
options: Swollen, painful glands in the cheeks and jaw
questions.expected: Swollen, painful glands in the cheeks and jaw
questions.memo: Mumps swells the salivary glands — face looks chipmunk-like. Spreads through saliva. The MMR vaccine prevents it.

questions.question: What is ATHLETE'S FOOT?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is athlete's foot?
options: A fungus that causes itchy, peeling skin between the toes
questions.expected: A fungus that causes itchy, peeling skin between the toes
questions.memo: Athlete's foot is a fungal infection. Loves warm, damp feet. Spreads through shared shower floors and towels. Anti-fungal creams treat it.

questions.question: True or false: VACCINATIONS prevent many communicable diseases.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Vaccinations prevent many communicable diseases.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Measles, mumps, polio, tetanus, hepatitis, TB — all preventable with vaccines. SA's free clinic vaccination programme has saved millions.

questions.question: What's the BEST way to prevent spreading colds and flu?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the best way to prevent spreading colds and flu?
options: Cover coughs/sneezes (into elbow), wash hands often, stay home when sick
questions.expected: Cover coughs/sneezes (into elbow), wash hands often, stay home when sick
questions.memo: Three simple habits. Each one breaks a link in the chain. Plus they protect others — community kindness.

questions.question: What causes TB (tuberculosis)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What causes TB — tuberculosis?
options: A bacterium that mainly attacks the lungs
questions.expected: A bacterium that mainly attacks the lungs
questions.memo: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Spreads through coughed-out droplets. Curable with medicine — free in SA.

questions.question: True or false: A cough lasting more than 2 weeks could be TB and needs a clinic visit.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A cough lasting more than 2 weeks could be TB and needs a clinic visit.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Two weeks is the warning signal. Clinics test for free. Caught early, TB is fully curable.

questions.question: Why is COVID-19 considered a communicable disease?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is COVID-19 considered a communicable disease?
options: It's caused by a virus that spreads from person to person via droplets
questions.expected: It's caused by a virus that spreads from person to person via droplets
questions.memo: COVID-19 is communicable through droplets and aerosols. Vaccines, distancing, masks and ventilation reduce spread. New variants keep emerging.

questions.question: What is the TREATMENT for most viral infections like colds?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the typical treatment for most viral infections like the common cold?
options: Rest, fluids, time — antibiotics don't work against viruses
questions.expected: Rest, fluids, time — antibiotics don't work against viruses
questions.memo: Antibiotics fight bacteria, NOT viruses. Misusing them creates 'superbugs' resistant to medicine. For colds: rest + fluids + paracetamol if needed.

questions.question: Sipho has a high fever and a rash. What should his family do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho has a high fever and a rash that's spreading. What should his family do?
options: Take him to the clinic — fever + rash needs proper diagnosis
questions.expected: Take him to the clinic — fever + rash needs proper diagnosis
questions.memo: Fever + rash could be measles, chickenpox, meningitis, or many other things. A clinic visit identifies it. Stay home meanwhile to avoid spreading.

questions.question: Which prevents athlete's foot?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these prevents athlete's foot?
options: Dry feet, clean socks, own towel, don't go barefoot in public showers
questions.expected: Dry feet, clean socks, own towel, don't go barefoot in public showers
questions.memo: Dry feet, own gear, footwear in shared wet areas. The fungus needs warm + damp — deny it that.

questions.question: Put these in order for handling a communicable disease in the family.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for handling a communicable disease in the family.
options: Take any medicine exactly as prescribed
Prevent spread to others (cover coughs, hand wash, own items)
questions.expected: Notice symptoms early,Visit a clinic for diagnosis,Take any medicine exactly as prescribed,Prevent spread to others (cover coughs, hand wash, own items)
questions.memo: Notice → diagnose → treat → prevent. Stopping the spread protects everyone you love.

questions.question: Why is it important to STAY HOME when you have a contagious illness?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to stay home when you have a contagious illness?
options: To stop spreading the illness to others, especially babies and elderly people
questions.expected: To stop spreading the illness to others, especially babies and elderly people
questions.memo: Babies and elderly people can get very sick from what's mild in healthy children. Staying home is a kindness — even when you feel okay.

questions.question: Tell me one communicable disease and one way to prevent it.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one communicable disease and one way to prevent it.
questions.expected: TB — cover your mouth when coughing
questions.memo: Good answers: cold (wash hands), TB (cover coughs, ventilate), measles (vaccine), chickenpox (vaccine, avoid the infected), athlete's foot (dry feet, own towel).

questions.question: True or false: Some communicable diseases (like measles) can be SERIOUS even though they seem common.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Some communicable diseases like measles can be very serious even though they seem common.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Measles can cause blindness, brain damage, death. That's why the measles vaccine matters so much. 'Common' ≠ 'mild'.

questions.question: Karabo's brother has TB. The family should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's brother has been diagnosed with TB. The family should:
options: Make sure he takes his medicine every day for the full course (usually 6 months)
Stop the medicine when he feels better
questions.expected: Make sure he takes his medicine every day for the full course (usually 6 months)
questions.memo: Skipping or stopping TB medicine creates drug-resistant TB — much harder to treat. The full course is essential. Free at SA clinics.

questions.question: Which is a way to reduce communicable diseases in a SCHOOL?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to reduce communicable diseases in a school?
options: Good hand-washing habits, ventilation, sick children stay home
questions.expected: Good hand-washing habits, ventilation, sick children stay home
questions.memo: Schools are major spread points. Hand-wash + open windows + sick days = lower transmission. Schools that do this have fewer absences overall.

questions.question: The big idea of stopping communicable diseases is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the big idea of stopping communicable diseases?
options: Prevention through hygiene + vaccines + early treatment + protecting the vulnerable
questions.expected: Prevention through hygiene + vaccines + early treatment + protecting the vulnerable
questions.memo: Public health works on four fronts. Hygiene at home. Vaccines free. Early treatment. Protecting babies and elderly. Together they save millions of lives.

LS.L6.PSW.T16.title: HIV and AIDS: myths and realities
LS.L6.PSW.T16.description: Myths and realities about HIV and AIDS including risks and perceptions; caring for people with AIDS.
LS.L6.PSW.T16.recovery_strategy: Replace myth with fact, gently. Don't shame anyone for past beliefs. Reinforce: people with HIV deserve full friendship; ARVs work; testing is free.

questions.question: MYTH: 'HIV can spread by hugging or shaking hands.' What's the REALITY?
questions.ruby_prompt: Myth: HIV can spread by hugging or shaking hands. What's the reality?
options: HIV does NOT spread through hugging, shaking hands, sharing food or other daily contact
questions.expected: HIV does NOT spread through hugging, shaking hands, sharing food or other daily contact
questions.memo: This is the most common HIV myth. The truth: HIV needs specific body fluids to spread. Daily contact is completely safe.

questions.question: MYTH: 'A person with HIV looks sick.' REALITY?
questions.ruby_prompt: Myth: A person with HIV looks sick. What's the reality?
options: People with HIV often look completely well, especially when on ARV treatment
questions.expected: People with HIV often look completely well, especially when on ARV treatment
questions.memo: You cannot tell who has HIV by looking. ARVs keep people healthy. Many SA adults are living long, well lives with HIV.

questions.question: MYTH: 'HIV can be cured by traditional herbs alone.' REALITY?
questions.ruby_prompt: Myth: HIV can be cured by traditional herbs alone. What's the reality?
options: HIV has no cure yet. ARVs CONTROL it so people live long healthy lives. Skipping ARVs for herbs alone is dangerous
Only the rich can be cured
questions.expected: HIV has no cure yet. ARVs CONTROL it so people live long healthy lives. Skipping ARVs for herbs alone is dangerous
questions.memo: False 'cures' cost SA lives in the past. The truth: there's no cure, but ARVs work brilliantly. Some traditional medicines can interact badly with ARVs.

questions.question: MYTH: 'HIV is a punishment for bad behaviour.' REALITY?
questions.ruby_prompt: Myth: HIV is a punishment for bad behaviour. What's the reality?
options: HIV is a virus, not a punishment. Many people get it through no fault of their own — including babies born to mothers with HIV
questions.expected: HIV is a virus, not a punishment. Many people get it through no fault of their own — including babies born to mothers with HIV
questions.memo: Viruses don't judge behaviour. Mothers, partners, medical workers, accident victims all can become HIV-positive. Stigma is wrong.

questions.question: MYTH: 'Mosquitoes spread HIV.' REALITY?
questions.ruby_prompt: Myth: Mosquitoes spread HIV. What's the reality?
options: Mosquitoes do NOT spread HIV. They spread malaria, but not HIV
questions.expected: Mosquitoes do NOT spread HIV. They spread malaria, but not HIV
questions.memo: HIV cannot survive or multiply inside mosquitoes. Malaria, dengue, yellow fever — yes. HIV — no.

questions.question: True or false: People with HIV on proper ARVs can live as long as anyone else.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: People with HIV on proper ARVs can live as long as anyone else.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. With consistent ARVs, life expectancy is similar to people without HIV. ARVs are one of the great medical successes of our time.

questions.question: What does CARING for someone with AIDS look like?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does caring for someone with AIDS look like?
options: Treating them with respect, helping with daily needs if asked, ensuring they get medicine, keeping their secret safe
questions.expected: Treating them with respect, helping with daily needs if asked, ensuring they get medicine, keeping their secret safe
questions.memo: Real care = respect first. Helping when asked, not taking over. Medicine, food, company, dignity. Privacy.

questions.question: MYTH: 'Sharing food spreads HIV.' REALITY?
questions.ruby_prompt: Myth: Sharing food spreads HIV. What's the reality?
options: Sharing food, cups, cutlery does NOT spread HIV. Saliva is not infectious enough
questions.expected: Sharing food, cups, cutlery does NOT spread HIV. Saliva is not infectious enough
questions.memo: HIV in saliva is far too little to infect. Sharing meals with someone with HIV is completely safe. Lots of stigma comes from this myth.

questions.question: Why is FREE HIV TESTING in SA so important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is free HIV testing in SA so important?
options: Knowing your status means you can start treatment early and protect those you love
questions.expected: Knowing your status means you can start treatment early and protect those you love
questions.memo: Test → know → treat → live well + don't spread. SA's free testing programme has changed millions of lives.

questions.question: Lerato's classmate has a mother with HIV. The right attitude is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerata's classmate has a mother with HIV. What's the right attitude?
options: Treat the classmate normally — having an HIV+ parent doesn't change who she is
Refuse to share food at school
questions.expected: Treat the classmate normally — having an HIV+ parent doesn't change who she is
questions.memo: Stigma touches families too. The classmate is just like anyone else. Friendship is the antidote to stigma.

questions.question: True or false: A mother with HIV on proper care can have an HIV-NEGATIVE baby.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A mother with HIV who gets proper care can have an HIV-negative baby.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. SA's mother-to-child prevention programme is one of the best in the world. Most babies of HIV+ moms are now born negative.

questions.question: Sipho's grandmother whispers, 'It's their own fault.' What can Sipho say?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's grandmother whispers about a neighbour with HIV, 'It's their own fault.' What can Sipho gently say?
options: 'Granny, HIV is a virus that anyone can get. The neighbour needs our care, not our judgement.'
questions.expected: 'Granny, HIV is a virus that anyone can get. The neighbour needs our care, not our judgement.'
questions.memo: Gentle truth-telling across generations is how stigma shifts. Sipho honours his grandmother AND corrects the false belief.

questions.question: What does U=U mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does U=U mean in HIV?
options: Undetectable = Untransmittable. When ARVs keep HIV very low, it cannot be passed on
questions.expected: Undetectable = Untransmittable. When ARVs keep HIV very low, it cannot be passed on
questions.memo: U=U is one of the most powerful HIV facts. Adherent ARV users with undetectable viral loads do not transmit HIV. Game-changer.

questions.question: Why might someone NOT disclose their HIV status?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might someone choose not to disclose their HIV status?
options: Fear of stigma — judgement, gossip, rejection, even job loss
questions.expected: Fear of stigma — judgement, gossip, rejection, even job loss
questions.memo: Stigma costs lives. People hide their status, skip clinics, lose families. Ending stigma = fewer deaths.

questions.question: Put these in order for SUPPORTING someone living with HIV.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for supporting someone living with HIV.
options: Help with practical things if needed (clinic visits, medicine reminders)
Stand up for them when others stigmatise
questions.expected: Listen and treat them normally,Respect their privacy,Help with practical things if needed (clinic visits, medicine reminders),Stand up for them when others stigmatise
questions.memo: Listen → privacy → practical care → allyship. Each step shows: you are valued, you are not alone, you are loved.

questions.question: Tell me one MYTH about HIV and the REALITY.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one myth about HIV and the reality.
questions.expected: Myth: HIV spreads by hugging. Reality: It does not spread by everyday contact
questions.memo: Good answers: any myth + correction. Mosquitoes/no; sharing food/safe; herbs cure/no, ARVs control; punishment/no, it's a virus.

questions.question: True or false: Stigma actively HARMS the fight against HIV in SA.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Stigma actively harms the fight against HIV in South Africa.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Stigma stops testing, skips treatment, breaks families. Ending stigma is part of ending HIV. Each kind word helps.

questions.question: World AIDS Day reminds the world to:
questions.ruby_prompt: World AIDS Day (1 December) reminds the world to:
options: Honour those who have died, support those living with HIV, push to end stigma and end HIV
questions.expected: Honour those who have died, support those living with HIV, push to end stigma and end HIV
questions.memo: Red ribbon = symbol of remembrance and support. SA marks World AIDS Day with services, education and clinics offering free testing.

questions.question: What HIV TRUTHS would help reduce stigma in SA?
questions.ruby_prompt: What HIV truths, widely shared, would help reduce stigma in SA?
options: It's a virus; it spreads in specific ways; ARVs control it; people with HIV live long lives
questions.expected: It's a virus; it spreads in specific ways; ARVs control it; people with HIV live long lives
questions.memo: Four key truths. When widely known and acted on, stigma shrinks. Each conversation moves us forward.

questions.question: The biggest TRUTH about HIV today is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the biggest truth about HIV today?
options: HIV is now a treatable, manageable condition — with care, people live full lives, free testing and ARVs are available in SA
HIV is contagious in every way
questions.expected: HIV is now a treatable, manageable condition — with care, people live full lives, free testing and ARVs are available in SA
questions.memo: We are not in the dark age of HIV anymore. Treatment works. Lives are full. Stigma is the remaining battle — and you can help end it.
